mainTopic: Several attempts to explain the משנה's 'כל האסורים לבוא בקהל' and רבי יהודה's dissent, ending with רבא's גר עמוני ומואבי reading, followed by a ברייתא on men who make a woman unfit for כהונה
overview: The גמרא keeps trying to explain the משנה's line that those 'forbidden to enter the קהל' may marry 'זה בזה', and what רבי יהודה disagrees with. First it reads the line as being about people forbidden to כהונה, such as a girl who converted before age three years and a day. Counterexamples knock that reading down. Next, רב נתן בר הושעיא reads it as being about anyone whose daughter a כהן may not marry. Cases of a חלל and of a גר break that reading too. רב נחמן then says the dispute is about a child born from a brother and sister. That is rejected because another משנה already argues that point. Finally, רבא explains that the משנה's permission is about a גר עמוני ומואבי. רבי יהודה forbids only a regular גר from marrying a ממזרת. The amud ends with a ברייתא listing men whose relations make a woman unfit to marry a כהן. רבי יוסי gives a narrower rule, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's opinion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Reading the משנה as referring to the priesthood
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's opening line is explained as: all those forbidden to marry into כהונה, such as a גיורת who converted before age three years and a day, are permitted to marry 'זה בזה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: all those who are forbidden to marry into the priesthood (who are they? For example, a girl who converted when she was younger than three years and one day, and this is not like רבי שמעון בן יוחי) are permitted to marry 'one another.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the משנה's first line really means. It says the line is talking about people who cannot marry a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'קהל' in the משנה is read as 'קהל כהונה', the congregation of the priesthood. The middle of the line is a side comment giving an example: a girl who converted very young. That example only works if we do not follow רבי שמעון בן יוחי, who allows such a girl to marry a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (the גמרא rereads a text)
The congregation of the priesthood (marrying a כהן)
A female convert
Who are they?
One another

steps.confusionAlert: The middle part ('who are they?') is a side comment. The main sentence is: 'All those forbidden to enter the priesthood are permitted to marry one another.'

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
All those forbidden to enter the congregation of the priesthood,
who are they?

phrases.aramaic: גִּיּוֹרֶת פְּחוּתָה מִבַּת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד,
phrases.english: a female convert younger than three years and one day,
and this is not like רבי שמעון בן יוחי,
are permitted to marry one another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation of the משנה's opening line from before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Those forbidden to כהונה, such as a girl who converted under three years and a day (not like רבי שמעון בן יוחי), may marry 'זה בזה'.

steps.title: Why not read it as an older convert so it fits everyone?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests explaining the case as a girl who converted at three years and a day or older, so that even רבי שמעון בן יוחי would agree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us explain it as a girl who converted at three years and one day, and then it fits even רבי שמעון בן יוחי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the example. It asks why we do not pick a case that everyone agrees with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that a girl who converted at three years and a day or older may not marry a כהן. If the משנה were talking about her, it would not have to go against רבי שמעון בן יוחי. The גמרא prefers readings that fit all opinions, so this is a real challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us explain it as talking about
And even

phrases.aramaic: וְנוֹקְמַהּ בְּבַת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד,
phrases.english: Let us explain it as a girl of three years and one day,
phrases.notes: He means a girl who converted at that age or older.

phrases.english: and then it fits even רבי שמעון בן יוחי!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the example chosen in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of an under-three convert as the example, which forces the reading to go against רבי שמעון בן יוחי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A reading that fits all opinions is better. An older convert is forbidden to כהונה according to everyone.

steps.title: That reading would make the משנה contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that if the case were an older convert, the משנה would break itself apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it breaks from its own side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers briefly that the suggested reading creates a contradiction inside the משנה. The next step explains how.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מצידה תברה' means the משנה would be knocked down by something it implies on its own. This short line sets up the explanation that comes right after it.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
It breaks from its own side, meaning it contradicts itself

phrases.english: If so, it breaks from its own side.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the suggested alternative reading fails on its own terms.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Reading the case as an older convert would let the משנה fit רבי שמעון בן יוחי.
steps.terutzMaskana: That reading creates an inner contradiction, so the example must be an under-three convert, not following רבי שמעון בן יוחי.

steps.title: Explaining the contradiction
steps.stepSummary: An older-convert reading would imply that a younger convert, who is permitted to כהונה, is forbidden 'זה בזה'. But according to רבי שמעון בן יוחי she is permitted to both.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is the reason only because she converted at three years and one day? Then a girl who converted younger than that, who is permitted to marry into the priesthood, would be forbidden to marry 'one another'? But according to רבי שמעון בן יוחי, a girl younger than three years and a day is permitted to the priesthood and also permitted to marry 'one another'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the contradiction it mentioned in step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה says the older convert may marry 'זה בזה' because she is forbidden to כהונה, we would infer that someone permitted to כהונה is forbidden 'זה בזה'. Yet רבי שמעון בן יוחי's young convert is permitted to both. So the משנה cannot be read according to him, and step 1's reading stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Is the reason only that
But then (introduces an inference)
But look, here is a case

steps.confusionAlert: Read the first half as a question showing what we would wrongly infer. The second half ('הרי') knocks that inference down.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא טַעְמָא דְּבַת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד,
phrases.english: Is the reason only because she is three years and one day,

phrases.aramaic: הָא פְּחוּתָה מִבַּת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד,
phrases.english: but then one younger than three years and one day,
who is permitted to enter the congregation of the priesthood,
is forbidden to marry 'one another'?

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי פְּחוּתָה מִבַּת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד
phrases.english: But here is one younger than three years and one day
according to רבי שמעון בן יוחי,
who is permitted to enter the congregation of the priesthood
and is also permitted to marry 'one another'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא טַעְמָא דְּבַת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the short answer of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the suggested reading leads to a false inference.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה could be about an older convert and fit רבי שמעון בן יוחי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Under that reading, רבי שמעון בן יוחי's young convert, who is permitted to both, would contradict the משנה's implication.
steps.whatToRemember: The example of a convert under three years and a day stays, and the משנה here does not follow רבי שמעון בן יוחי.

steps.title: Women forbidden to a כהן are not free to marry flawed families
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule itself: אלמנה, גרושה, חללה, and זונה are forbidden to כהונה, yet they are also forbidden 'זה בזה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really a rule that all those forbidden to enter the priesthood are permitted to marry one another? But a widow, a divorcée, a חללה, and a זונה are forbidden to the priesthood, and they are also forbidden to marry 'one another'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks the general rule from step 1, using counterexamples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1's reading turns the משנה into a broad rule: anyone forbidden to כהונה may marry 'זה בזה'. The גמרא points to four women who are forbidden to כהונה but are still not permitted 'זה בזה'. So the rule cannot be stated that broadly.

keyTerms.meaning: A general rule
A widow (forbidden to a כהן גדול)
A divorced woman
A woman disqualified from marrying a כהן
A woman who had relations forbidden to her by the Torah

phrases.english: And is it a general rule
that all those forbidden to enter the congregation of the priesthood
are permitted to marry one another?
But there are a widow, a divorcée, a חללה, and a זונה
who are forbidden to enter the congregation of the priesthood,
and are forbidden to marry one another!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְלָלָא הוּא דְּכׇל הָאֲסוּרִים לָבֹא בִּקְהַל כְּהוּנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the example to challenge the general rule of step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that everyone forbidden to כהונה is permitted 'זה בזה'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counterexamples: four kinds of women are forbidden to כהונה but not permitted 'זה בזה'.

steps.title: A גר is permitted to both a כהנת and a ממזרת
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge: the rule implies that whoever is permitted to כהונה is forbidden 'זה בזה', but a גר is permitted to both a כהנת and a ממזרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: does this imply that one who is permitted is forbidden? But a convert is permitted to a כהן's daughter and also permitted to a ממזרת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second challenge, this time from the flip side of the rule. The next step responds by dropping this reading and offering a new one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'forbidden to כהונה' leads to 'permitted זה בזה', the reverse seems to follow: 'permitted to כהונה' leads to 'forbidden זה בזה'. A גר breaks this, since he may marry a כהנת and may also marry a ממזרת. Together with step 5, this knocks down the reading, and step 7 replaces it.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore
A male convert
A daughter of a כהן
A female ממזר

phrases.english: And furthermore: does this imply that one who is permitted is forbidden?
phrases.notes: He means: permitted to the priesthood, so forbidden to marry 'one another'.

phrases.english: But there is a convert, who is permitted to a כהן's daughter
and is also permitted to a ממזרת!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge to the rule, from the reverse side.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implied reverse of the rule: whoever is permitted to כהונה is forbidden 'זה בזה'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גר is permitted to a כהנת and also to a ממזרת, which breaks the implied reverse rule.

steps.title: A new reading: whoever's daughter a priest cannot marry
steps.stepSummary: רב נתן בר הושעיא reads the rule as being about people whose daughters a כהן may not marry, such as a גר who married a גיורת according to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. Such people may marry 'זה בזה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נתן בר הושעיא said: This is what it means. Anyone whose daughter a כהן may not marry (for example, a convert who married a convert, according to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב) may marry into the families that are blocked from the קהל.
steps.whatsHappening: Steps 5 and 6 knocked down the old reading, so the גמרא offers a brand-new way to understand the rule. Now it is about people whose daughters a כהן cannot marry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new test is not whether the person himself may marry into כהונה. It is whether a כהן may marry his daughter. The example is a family made up only of converts. According to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, their daughter may not marry a כהן. Converts are not counted as part of the 'קהל', so they may marry families like ממזרים.

keyTerms.meaning: A male convert to Judaism
A female convert to Judaism
A תנא who holds that a daughter of two converts may not marry a כהן
'This one with that one': marrying into the families that may not enter the קהל

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'אסור' describes the daughter and the כהן, not the person himself. Don't mix this up with the old reading from the earlier steps, which asked whether the person himself may marry into כהונה.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נָתָן בַּר הוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Natan bar Hoshaya said:
This is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁכֹּהֵן אָסוּר לִישָּׂא אֶת בִּתּוֹ,
phrases.english: Anyone whose daughter a priest may not marry,
and who is that? A convert who married a female convert,
and this follows Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov;
such people are permitted to marry one another.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נָתָן בַּר הוֹשַׁעְיָא הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the reading that steps 5 and 6 knocked down
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule is about whether the person himself may marry into כהונה
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule is about whether a כהן may marry the person's daughter

steps.title: Challenge from a חלל who married an ordinary Jewish woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether this is really a rule. A כהן may not marry the daughter of a חלל and a בת ישראל, yet that family may not marry 'זה בזה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really a rule that anyone whose daughter a כהן may not marry may marry 'זה בזה'? Take a חלל who married a Jewish woman. A כהן may not marry his daughter, yet they are also forbidden to marry 'זה בזה'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the new rule with a counter-example. Here a כהן cannot marry the daughter, but the family still may not marry ממזרים and the like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חלל and his family are full members of the קהל, so they may not marry ממזרים. But his daughter is a חללה, so a כהן may not marry her. That breaks the new rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A son of a כהן born from a marriage forbidden to a כהן, who does not have כהונה status
An ordinary Jewish woman
A general rule

phrases.english: But is it a rule

phrases.aramaic: דְּכׇל שֶׁכֹּהֵן אָסוּר לִישָּׂא אֶת בִּתּוֹ
phrases.english: that anyone whose daughter a priest may not marry
is permitted to marry one another?
But there is a חלל who married a Jewish woman,
whose daughter a priest may not marry,
and they are also forbidden to marry one another!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְלָלָא הוּא דְּכׇל שֶׁכֹּהֵן אָסוּר לִישָּׂא אֶת בִּתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב נתן בר הושעיא's new rule
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that whoever's daughter a כהן may not marry may marry 'זה בזה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A counter-example: a case where a כהן may not marry the daughter, yet the family is forbidden 'זה בזה'

steps.title: Answer: this follows רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the rule follows רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה. According to him, a כהן may marry the daughter of a חלל and a בת ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is not difficult. The rule follows רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the rule by saying it follows a תנא for whom the counter-example does not apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה, a חלל's daughter from a בת ישראל is fit to marry a כהן. So this case does not fall under the rule at all, and the problem goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not difficult': the question has an answer
A תנא who holds that the daughter of a חלל and a בת ישראל may marry a כהן

phrases.english: It is not difficult;
it follows Rabbi Dostai ben Yehuda.
phrases.notes: According to him, a כהן may marry this girl, so this case doesn't break the rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא כְּרַבִּי דּוֹסְתַּאי בֶּן יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ties the rule to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A כהן may not marry the daughter of a חלל and a בת ישראל
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה she may marry a כהן, so the counter-example does not apply

steps.title: Challenge from a חלל who married a חללה
steps.stepSummary: Even according to רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה, a כהן may not marry the daughter of a חלל and a חללה. Yet that family is still forbidden 'זה בזה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But take a חלל who married a חללה. A כהן may not marry his daughter, and they are also forbidden to marry 'זה בזה'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a stronger counter-example that the answer in step 9 cannot get around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When both parents are חללים, the daughter is a חללה even according to רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה. These people are still part of the קהל, so they may not marry ממזרים. The rule breaks again.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman unfit to marry a כהן because of a forbidden priestly marriage

phrases.english: But there is a חלל who married a חללה,
and a priest may not marry his daughter,
and he is also forbidden to marry one another!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gets around the answer from step 9 with a case that רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה would also forbid
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נתן בר הושעיא's rule, even as answered in step 9
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even רבי דוסתאי בן יהודה agrees this daughter may not marry a כהן, yet the family may not marry 'זה בזה'

steps.title: Second challenge: the flip side of the rule fails too
steps.stepSummary: The rule implies that if a כהן may marry someone's daughter, that person may not marry 'זה בזה'. But a גר who married a בת ישראל has a daughter a כהן may marry, and he may still marry 'זה בזה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: does it follow that whoever is permitted is forbidden? Take a גר who married a Jewish woman. A כהן may marry his daughter, and they may still marry 'זה בזה'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule from the other side, by looking at what it implies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'a כהן may not marry his daughter' means 'he may marry זה בזה', then the flip side should be: 'a כהן may marry his daughter' means 'he may not'. A גר married to a בת ישראל breaks this. A כהן may marry his daughter, yet as a גר he is not part of the קהל and may marry ממזרים. So the rule fails in both directions.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And furthermore': brings an additional challenge
'So the permitted one is forbidden?': a challenge from what the rule implies

steps.whatToRemember: Steps 8 to 11 together show that 'whether a כהן may marry his daughter' cannot be the test for marrying 'זה בזה'. It fails in both directions.

phrases.english: And furthermore: does it follow that one who is permitted is forbidden?
phrases.notes: He means: if a כהן may marry this man's daughter, does the rule mean the man himself may not marry 'זה בזה'?

phrases.english: But there is a convert who married a Jewish woman,
and a priest is permitted to marry his daughter,
and they are permitted to marry one another!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge, based on what the rule implies
steps.kashyaTarget: The implied flip side of רב נתן בר הושעיא's rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule implies that if a כהן may marry the daughter, the person is forbidden 'זה בזה'. A גר who married a בת ישראל disproves this.

steps.title: A new explanation: the dispute is about two kinds of ממזר
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, in the name of רבה בר אבוה, drops the earlier approach. He says the real difference between the two sides is a ממזר born from a man and his sister versus a ממזר born from a married woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: Here, the difference between them is a ממזר from a man's sister and a ממזר from a married woman.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the rule-based reading fell apart, the גמרא starts over with a completely different explanation of what the dispute is about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of a general rule about who may marry 'זה בזה', the disagreement now turns on how a ממזר was born. One kind comes from a forbidden relationship with a sister. The other comes from a relationship with a married woman.

keyTerms.meaning: A child born from certain forbidden relationships, who may not marry into the קהל
A married woman
'There is between them': this is the point where the two opinions differ

steps.whatToRemember: The search for a simple rule failed. The dispute is now explained as being about different kinds of ממזר.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
Here, a ממזר from a man and his sister
and a ממזר from a married woman
is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Drops רב נתן בר הושעיא's reading after it was disproved and gives a new explanation of the dispute
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines what the dispute is about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute turns on a general rule about whose daughter a כהן may marry
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute is about a ממזר from a sister versus a ממזר from a married woman

steps.title: Spelling out the two sides of רב נחמן's explanation
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא holds that a child born from a brother and sister is a ממזר. רבי יהודה holds that only a child from an אשת איש is a ממזר, and a child from a sister is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first תנא holds that even a child born from a man and his sister is a ממזר. רבי יהודה holds that a child from a married woman is a ממזר, but a child from a man's sister is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues רב נחמן's answer from the last step. It now explains exactly what each side holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, both kinds of children are ממזרים, so they may marry each other. For רבי יהודה, the child from a sister is not a ממזר, so he may not marry a real ממזר. That is why רבי יהודה forbids them to marry each other.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא
A child born from certain forbidden unions, who may not marry an ordinary Jew
His sister
A married woman

phrases.english: The first tanna holds:
Even a mamzer from his sister
is also a mamzer.
And Rabbi Yehuda holds:
From a married woman, he is a mamzer;
from his sister, he is not a mamzer.
phrases.notes: So for רבי יהודה, this child is not a ממזר and may not marry one, which is why he forbids the two groups to marry 'זה בזה'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב נחמן's answer from step 12 by stating what each side holds.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the point of the מחלוקת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מחלוקת was explained using the rule 'whoever's daughter a כהן may not marry', which ran into problems.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מחלוקת is about whether a child from a brother and sister is a ממזר.

steps.title: This was already taught in another משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב נחמן's reading adds. A משנה elsewhere already records a מחלוקת about which unions make a ממזר: רבי עקיבא, שמעון התימני and רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this teaching us? We already learned: Who is a ממזר? Any child from a union forbidden by 'לא יבא'. These are the words of רבי עקיבא. שמעון התימני says: any child from a union punished with כרת at the hands of Heaven, and the הלכה follows him. רבי יהושע says: any child from a union punished with death by בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב נחמן's explanation. It points out that the question of whether a brother-sister union makes a ממזר is already argued in another משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A brother-sister union carries כרת, not death by בית דין. So שמעון התימני would say the child is a ממזר, and רבי יהושע would say he is not. Our משנה would just repeat that same argument, so רב נחמן's reading leaves it with nothing new to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this teaching us? (asked when something seems already known)
We have already learned this in a משנה
Being cut off, a punishment that comes from Heaven
The death penalty given by a court

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying רב נחמן's ruling is wrong. It is saying that if our משנה only meant this, it would just be repeating another משנה.

phrases.english: What is it teaching us?
We already learned:
Who is a mamzer?
Anyone who comes from a union under 'he shall not enter',
phrases.notes: דברים 23:3. רבי עקיבא counts every forbidden union in the Torah, even one without כרת.

phrases.english: These are the words of Rabbi Akiva.
Shimon HaTimni says:
Anyone from a union for which one is liable to
karet at the hand of Heaven,
and the halakha follows his words.
Rabbi Yehoshua says:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁחַיָּיבִין עָלָיו מִיתַת בֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: Anyone from a union for which one is liable to court-imposed death.
phrases.notes: A brother and sister get כרת, not death by בית דין, so for רבי יהושע their child is not a ממזר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's explanation from steps 12 and 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that the מחלוקת is about a ממזר from a sister versus one from an אשת איש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redundancy: another משנה already argues about whether a כרת-level union produces a ממזר. Our משנה would add nothing.

steps.title: רבא: the argument is about an עמוני and מואבי convert
steps.stepSummary: רבא drops רב נחמן's approach. He says the difference between the תנא קמא and רבי יהודה is a גר עמוני ומואבי. The תנא קמא's words 'all those forbidden to enter the קהל' refer to them, and they may marry 'זה בזה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: The difference between them is an עמוני or מואבי convert. This is what the תנא is saying: All those forbidden to enter the קהל, and who are they? An עמוני or מואבי convert. They are permitted to marry one another.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב נחמן's reading was rejected, רבא gives a brand-new explanation of the מחלוקת in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads the תנא קמא's phrase 'those forbidden to enter the קהל' as describing a male גר עמוני ומואבי. According to the תנא קמא, they may marry the others in those groups. This gives our משנה something new to teach, avoiding the problem in step 14. Step 16 asks what רבי יהודה's 'forbidding' could then mean, and step 17 explains it.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier answer and starts a new one)
A male convert from עמון or מואב, who may not marry into the קהל
There is a difference between them
To marry into the Jewish people
With one another

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן's approach (a ממזר from a sister) is rejected because it repeats an existing משנה. רבא explains the מחלוקת as being about a גר עמוני ומואבי.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
An Ammonite and Moabite convert
is the difference between them,
and this is what it is saying:
All those forbidden to enter the congregation,
and who are they? An Ammonite and Moabite convert,
are permitted to marry one another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 14 by replacing רב נחמן's explanation with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New explanation of the משנה's subject (אלא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מחלוקת was about whether a child from a brother and sister is a ממזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מחלוקת is about a גר עמוני ומואבי. According to the תנא קמא, they may marry 'זה בזה'.

steps.title: Then what is רבי יהודה forbidding?
steps.stepSummary: If the תנא קמא's permission is about a גר עמוני ומואבי, the גמרא asks what רבי יהודה's prohibition is about.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is רבי יהודה forbidding?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's reading. If the תנא קמא is speaking about a גר עמוני ומואבי, it is unclear what רבי יהודה disagrees with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said the תנא קמא's phrase 'all those forbidden to enter the קהל' refers to a גר עמוני ומואבי. They are also not fit to enter the קהל, so it seems רבי יהודה should agree they may marry a ממזרת. So it is unclear what his 'forbidding' is about.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if you explain it this way
Forbids

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: He means: if רבא is right that the תנא קמא is talking about a גר עמוני ומואבי.

phrases.english: what is Rabbi Yehuda forbidding?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי מַאי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹסֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's reading from step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading that the תנא קמא is speaking about a גר עמוני ומואבי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גר עמוני ומואבי is not fit to enter the קהל either, so רבי יהודה would seem to have nothing to argue about.

steps.title: רבי יהודה forbids only a regular convert
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה forbids a regular גר, who may enter the קהל, from marrying a ממזרת. He agrees that a גר עמוני ומואבי may marry her.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: even though רבי יהודה forbids a גר to marry a ממזרת, that applies only to a גר who is fit to enter the קהל. A גר עמוני ומואבי, who is not fit to enter the קהל, is not forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה's prohibition covers only a regular גר. On the גר עמוני ומואבי, he agrees with the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read this way, רבי יהודה's words are an 'even though' statement and not a disagreement on this case. A regular גר may marry into the קהל, so he may not marry a ממזרת. A גר עמוני ומואבי may not marry into the קהל anyway, so marrying a ממזרת is permitted to him.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means; a re-reading of the words
A female ממזר
This applies only to
Fit to marry into the Jewish people

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, everyone agrees that a גר עמוני ומואבי may marry a ממזרת. רבי יהודה forbids only a regular גר.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹסֵר
phrases.english: Even though Rabbi Yehuda forbids
a convert with a mamzeret,
that applies only to a convert
who is fit to enter the congregation,
but an Ammonite or Moabite convert
who are not fit to enter the congregation, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading רבי יהודה's words as limited to a regular גר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה seemed to disagree with the תנא קמא about a גר עמוני ומואבי.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה forbids only a regular גר who may enter the קהל. He agrees that a גר עמוני ומואבי may marry a ממזרת.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists men who make a woman unfit for a כהן
steps.stepSummary: A boy of nine years and one day from any of these groups makes a woman unfit to marry a כהן if he has relations with her: גר עמוני ומואבי, מצרי, אדומי, כותי, נתין, חלל or ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: if a boy nine years and one day old who is a גר עמוני ומואבי, a מצרי or אדומי, a כותי or נתין, a חלל or ממזר, had relations with a כהנת, a לויה or a בת ישראל, he made her unfit to marry a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא. It lists men who are unfit to marry into the קהל and rules that relations with any of them make a woman unfit to marry a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Age nine years and one day is the age at which a boy's relations count legally. The list covers several kinds of men who are unfit to marry into the קהל. The ruling applies to a woman from any family: כהן, לוי or ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught; this introduces a ברייתא
A boy nine years and one day old
A Samaritan
A descendant of the גבעונים
A son of a כהן from a marriage forbidden to a כהן
They made her unfit to marry a כהן

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A boy nine years and one day old
who is an Ammonite or Moabite convert,
an Egyptian or Edomite,
a Samaritan or a Gibeonite,
a chalal or a mamzer,
who had relations with the daughter of a priest,
or the daughter of a Levite, or an Israelite woman,
they have disqualified her.
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have this word; the corrected wording adds it. It means she may no longer marry a כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא about men who make a woman unfit for כהונה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relations with any of these men make a woman unfit to marry a כהן.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: it depends on whether the man's children are unfit
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says only a man whose children are unfit makes the woman unfit. A man whose children are not unfit does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: anyone whose children are unfit makes her unfit, and anyone whose children are not unfit does not make her unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי disagrees with the first opinion in the ברייתא. He gives his own rule for which men make a woman unfit to marry a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion makes every man on the list disqualify the woman. רבי יוסי's test is narrower: it looks at whether this man's children would be unfit. If his children would be fine, his relations do not make her unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: His children; his descendants
Makes unfit; disqualifies

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
anyone whose offspring is unfit disqualifies,
phrases.notes: Unfit here means unfit to marry a כהן.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵין זַרְעוֹ פָּסוּל – אֵינוֹ פּוֹסֵל.
phrases.english: and anyone whose offspring is not unfit does not disqualify.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a disagreeing opinion within the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man makes the woman unfit only if his children would be unfit.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל begins his opinion
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא introduces a third opinion, from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. His words continue in the next part of the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says:
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. The ברייתא is about to give רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view, and his actual words come right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are now two opinions on the table: the first opinion of the ברייתא and רבי יוסי. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is about to add a third view on which men make a woman unfit to marry a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who gives a third opinion in this ברייתא

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a third opinion in the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: His ruling comes on the next amud.
